Container.Name: openbot
Container.Overview:
OpenBot runs your AI coding and computer-use agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Cursor, Grok and more) as an always-on self-hosted server. You use it from the OpenBot desktop app, the iPhone app or https://openbot.run/app with the same account. The container publishes no port: it only connects out (to openbot.run, your AI providers, and Signal/TURN relays for remote access).
**Before the first start (required)**
Run this in the Unraid terminal. It downloads the seccomp profile OpenBot needs for its Electron sandbox and gives the data folder to the image's user (uid 1000):
`mkdir -p /mnt/user/appdata/openbot/data` `curl -fsSL -o /mnt/user/appdata/openbot/seccomp.json https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nightly-labs/openbot/main/docker/seccomp.json` `chown 1000:1000 /mnt/user/appdata/openbot/data` `chmod 700 /mnt/user/appdata/openbot/data`
Without the profile the container stops with "cannot make a user namespace". If the folder is not owned by 1000 it stops with "User 1000 cannot write to /data". Do not use `seccomp=unconfined` or Privileged instead.
**Sign in**
1. Start the container, then run `docker exec -it openbot openbot login` (email and emailed code). 2. Open the OpenBot app with the same account and connect a provider (Claude Code, Codex...). 3. Phone: `docker exec -it openbot openbot mobile-connect` and scan the QR code (valid 2 minutes). `openbot status` shows the version, account and memory limits.
**Notes**
- Extra Parameters hold upstream's required options: seccomp profile, no-new-privileges, 1 GB shared memory (Chromium), a 60 s stop timeout (OpenBot closes its database cleanly) and `--restart=unless-stopped` (the app exits on purpose when you restart it from Server Settings). - Updates come from pulling a new image. Never roll back to an older tag: newer versions migrate the database. Re-check `docker/seccomp.json` after big updates. - Agents have full access inside the container. Do not map the Docker socket or shares the agents must not change. Install extra tools into `~/.local` (on PATH) so they survive updates. - Host network is optional (LAN clients connect directly instead of through TURN), but the container will not start if Unraid runs its own GUI display. - Self-hosted account server: add a variable `OPENBOT_AUTH_API_URL` (HTTPS). Do not add it empty, because OpenBot rejects an empty URL. - Licence: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0.
Docker guide: https://github.com/nightly-labs/openbot/blob/main/docs/docker.md

Container.Requires: seccomp.json downloaded to /mnt/user/appdata/openbot/ and the data folder owned by 1000:1000 (see Overview) An openbot.run account

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Everything OpenBot keeps: database, conversations, agent workspaces, browser data, provider sign-ins and keyring. Must be owned by 1000:1000 (see Overview). Keep it as one unit and back it up with the container stopped.

Config.Name: Agent Display Size
Config.Description: Size of the virtual display agents use for computer use, WIDTHxHEIGHT from 640x480 to 2576x2576.

Config.Name: xAI API Key
Config.Description: Optional provider key for Grok. Agents can read every variable set here.

Config.Name: Setup Page Port
Config.Description: Optional (1024-65535, e.g. 8080). Starts a browser setup page for signing in the server; you must also add a matching Port mapping. Anyone who reaches it can sign in a signed-out server, so only expose it behind a password-protected proxy.
